subject: Exec update: SDK parity audit — breaking changes + release approach
body:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 8:12 AM PT
Subject: Exec update: SDK parity audit — breaking changes + release approach

Monica / Nikhil — quick exec update on the SDK parity audit work (Python/TS/Go) and what we expect to ship. TL;DR: a few behavior changes will be user-visible; we have a mitigation + comms plan to avoid surprises and reduce support load.

What’s changing (user-visible)
1) Retries (default behavior)
- We’re standardizing retry-on: 429, select 5xx, and transport errors.
- Backoff becomes exponential w/ jitter + a retry budget to avoid amplification.
- Impact: TS customers currently seeing “retry storms” on 429 should improve; Python/Go customers who previously had no retries in some paths may see additional attempts.

2) Timeouts (default behavior)
- Standardize connect/read/overall defaults and align semantics across languages.
- Impact: a small set of customers relying on “effectively infinite” timeouts may see earlier failures; we’ll document and provide easy override.

3) Streaming disconnect handling
- SSE parsing hardening + consistent cancellation semantics.
- Clear rule: we do NOT auto-resume streams (to avoid duplicate partial outputs); mid-stream disconnect surfaces a specific error w/ request-id for support.
- Impact: customers currently “getting lucky” with implicit reconnect in one SDK may need to handle reconnect at app level.

4) Auth config clarity
- Consistent API key discovery order + consistent header name.
- Explicit missing-key error messaging w/ remediation.
- Impact: should reduce enterprise security review friction; small risk of breaking customers using non-standard env var names (we can keep compatibility aliases for a deprecation window).

Release approach (proposed)
- Prefer minor/patch releases where possible; reserve majors only if we must remove an old behavior without compatibility shims.
- Provide per-request/per-client overrides for retry + timeout for advanced users.
- Add prominent migration notes + a single “SDK Client Behavior Standard” doc to anchor future behavior.

Customer impact mitigation
- Staged rollout by SDK (Python -> Go -> TS) with a 1–2 week gap, watching support tickets + metrics.
- “Escape hatch” config for conservative customers: disable retries entirely and/or set previous timeout semantics.
- Changelog entries include “Behavior change” callouts + concrete examples.
- Support-ready artifacts: recommended client configs + troubleshooting guide (request-id, retry-after guidance).

Asks / decision points
- Do we have a strong preference to avoid major versions in any SDK even if behavior changes? (We can keep compatibility aliases for auth env vars and keep old defaults behind a flag, but that increases complexity.)
- Any top accounts you want us to proactively warn (via CS) for streaming + timeout changes?

Attachments:
- SDK_Parity_Release_Plan_v1.pdf
- Customer_Impact_Summary_SDK_Parity_v0.3.docx

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Program Management (Eng)
Redwood Inference


From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: SDK parity audit — breaking changes + release approach

Thanks. Two concerns:

1) Streaming: we need to be crisp that we won’t auto-resume and why (duplicate output risk). Make sure support + docs have that language.

2) Retries: want to ensure we don’t regress into retry amplification, especially on 429. Please confirm SRE sign-off on defaults + retry budget.

On majors: I’d rather not do major bumps unless we truly remove an existing public API. Behavior changes w/ clear comms + overrides feel acceptable as minor in most ecosystems, but we need consistent guidance.

Monica


From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: SDK parity audit — breaking changes + release approach

+1 to Monica.

From product side:
- Please keep this out of “surprise breaking change” territory for the hosted API. If we can ship defaults that reduce support issues without forcing app changes, that’s ideal.
- For timeouts: we should call out that streaming timeouts differ from non-streaming, and recommend explicit values in quickstarts.
- For auth: keep compatibility aliases for at least one release cycle, and log a non-fatal warning (redacted) when someone uses deprecated env vars.

Henry — we should draft a single set of release notes language that applies across SDKs.

Nikhil


From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:04 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: SDK parity audit — breaking changes + release approach

Got it. Proposed decisions based on your guidance:

1) Streaming
- We’ll explicitly document: no auto-resume/reconnect mid-stream by default (duplicate tokens / partial tool calls / non-idempotent semantics).
- Error will include request-id and a stable error code so support can correlate quickly.

2) Retries (SRE safety)
- Ibrahim confirmed Rafael/Tomáš reviewed the draft defaults (ADR-0137): jitter required; capped attempts; retry budget; honor Retry-After on 429 when present.
- Also adding a client-side hook for telemetry so we can detect retry amplification (attempt count + final status) without logging secrets.

3) Semver
- No majors planned at this time.
- We will keep compatibility aliases for auth env vars for one release cycle, plus a redacted warning.
- For customers who need previous behavior: we’ll provide a documented config to disable retries and set timeouts explicitly.

4) Rollout + comms
- Henry/I will align on release notes language + a short “What changed / What to do” section per SDK.
- We’ll ask CS to proactively alert any accounts with known streaming issues (TS disconnects) and any accounts currently using long-lived streams behind proxies.

Next steps
- We’ll treat the above as baseline for PM-611 messaging.
- Target: ship Python/Go first, then TS, with a monitoring checkpoint between.

Thanks,
Alex
